name: window-management-plus
title: Window Management+
description: Companion to Raycast's Window Management, inspired by Hyprland. Tile every open window at once with master and grid layouts, swap, rotate, and move windows between displays. Requires Raycast Pro.
author: connorforsyth

preferences.name: sidebar
preferences.title: Sidebar
preferences.description: Window pinned full height down the right by Auto Tile with Sidebar.

commands.name: auto-tile
commands.title: Auto Tile
commands.description: Arrange every visible window in two even rows, or columns after Toggle Split.

commands.name: auto-tile-sidebar
commands.title: Auto Tile with Sidebar
commands.description: Pin the sidebar app (Raycast Notes by default) full height down the right and tile every other visible window.

commands.name: smart-arrange
commands.title: Smart Arrange
commands.description: Arrange windows by what each app is for. The focused window leads the largest display with your other work beside it. Chat, mail and music go to the other display.

commands.name: toggle-split
commands.title: Toggle Split
commands.description: Switch Auto Tile between rows and columns.

commands.name: master-left
commands.title: Master Layout Left
commands.description: The focused window becomes the master on the left. The rest stack on the right.

commands.name: master-right
commands.title: Master Layout Right
commands.description: The focused window becomes the master on the right. The rest stack on the left.

commands.name: master-center
commands.title: Master Layout Center
commands.description: The focused window becomes the master in the middle. The rest stack on both sides. Made for wide displays.

commands.name: grow-master
commands.title: Grow Master
commands.description: Give the master window more of the screen, in steps of 5%.

commands.name: shrink-master
commands.title: Shrink Master
commands.description: Give the master window less of the screen, in steps of 5%.

commands.name: swap-with-master
commands.title: Swap with Master
commands.description: Trade places between the active window and the master, the biggest window in the layout.

commands.name: swap-next
commands.title: Swap with Next Window
commands.description: Trade places between the focused window and the next one round. Two windows simply swap, whether they sit side by side or stacked.

commands.name: rotate
commands.title: Rotate Windows Clockwise
commands.description: Move every window one slot clockwise, keeping the last layout you tiled with.

commands.name: rotate-backwards
commands.title: Rotate Windows Counterclockwise
commands.description: Move every window one slot counterclockwise, keeping the last layout you tiled with.

commands.name: swap-displays
commands.title: Swap Displays
commands.description: Move every window to the other display. They land in the last layout you tiled with, or keep their place on the screen if you haven't tiled. With more than two displays, each display's windows move to the next.

commands.name: distribute-displays
commands.title: Distribute Across Displays
commands.description: Spread your windows over every display, a share for each by size and no more than each can fit, then tile each display with the last layout you used.

commands.name: move-others
commands.title: Move Others to Next Display
commands.description: Keep the focused window on its display and move every other window there to the next display, tiled with the last layout you used.

commands.name: move-all
commands.title: Move All to This Display
commands.description: Move every window from your other displays to the display with the focused window, tiled with the last layout you used.

commands.name: toggle-menu-bar-visibility
commands.title: Toggle Menu Bar Visibility
commands.description: Hide or show the menu bar.

tools.name: get-windows
tools.title: Get Windows
tools.description: List every display and every open window on the current desktop, with its app, title, display and frame.

tools.name: arrange-windows
tools.title: Arrange Windows
tools.description: Move windows onto chosen displays in a chosen order and tile each display with a chosen layout.

ai.instructions:
You arrange the user's open windows so they suit what the user is doing.
Always call get-windows first, then call arrange-windows once with a plan for every display.
Work out the task from the apps, window titles and each window's role (work, reference, comms or background). Put the window the user is working in (usually the focused one, or the editor, document or design tool) first on the largest display, and use a master layout when one window clearly matters most.
Keep related windows together on one display, such as an editor with its terminal and browser preview.
Put supporting windows such as chat, music, mail, notes and settings on the smaller display, or last in the order.
A display fits about three windows side by side when it is under 1600 points wide, and about six when it is wider. Do not give a display more than that unless there is nowhere else to put them.
Use auto-tile when the windows matter equally. Use master-center only on displays wider than 2000 points.
After arranging, say in one or two sentences what you put where and why. Do not list frames or ids.
